origin.finding: I-00-B's binding.json binds only isolated_binding_plan and command_binding_rule; it has no checkout path and no materialised-copy hash, while card text at M17-M20 line 49 says 'read the isolated checkout from I-00-B'.
reviewer_options: (a) owner ratifies in writing that materialisation is per-attempt and records the source hash
(b) re-run B/C/E so I-00-B actually materialises a checkout
origin.why_option_a: Option (b) would re-run three already-sealed attempts, creating a new evidence generation and invalidating existing hash registrations, while the measured code bytes are identical. Burning high-risk means on a pure documentation gap is the wrong trade; option (a) only requires describing the existing, already-verified division of labour truthfully.

deliverable.conclusion: the ratified sentence is true on disk; this card issues the ratification record and proves the three halves
deliverable.ratification_text: I-00-B binds the isolation plan and the two-stage command rule; it does not materialise a checkout tree. Materialisation is performed by each attempt, which materialises its own read-only snapshot (iso/checkout_scripts) and records the production hashes it was copied from. Each attempt's measured snapshot is byte-identical to production.

R-1.claim: the factual basis holds: I-00-B binds the plan but contains no checkout path and no materialised-copy hash

R-2.claim: each affected attempt materialises its own read-only snapshot

R-3.claim: each affected attempt records the source hash it copied from

R-4.claim: the recorded snapshots equal production byte-for-byte
R-4.evidence: 10/10 snapshots' model_registry.py recompute to 9ec6529550f189a435aed2eaba9b915bc104736f3d660049b9e3999f6ee2d17f, the production anchor

key_findings: F-T20-1: the ratification's premise is true - I-00-B binds the isolation plan and the two-stage command rule, has no checkout path, and its only 64-hex strings are source_anchors_sha256 (anchors, not copies).
F-T20-2: all 10 affected cards (M13, M14, M17-M24) materialise their own iso/checkout_scripts snapshot; the ratified division of labour is real.

F-T20-3: all 10 record the production hashes they copied from, and every snapshot's model_registry.py recomputes to the production anchor 9ec65295..., so 'byte-identical to production' is measured, not asserted.
F-T20-4: M24/binding.json:11 already carries the ratification sentence verbatim in English - the per-attempt materialisation note was written by the attempts themselves before the owner ratified it.
limits: R-2/R-3/R-4 sample the 10 cards the reviewer named. They do not exhaustively prove the stronger claim 'every attempt in the plan does this'. The ratified sentence says 'each attempt'; what is proven is that it holds for the named attempts. Claiming more than the method supports is the overreach this project's discipline forbids.
why_not_write_the_ratification_into_i00b: The owner's ruling is a written ratification. Writing it into I-00-B's attempt directory would post-hoc change what the reviewer was asked to review - that attempt is already accepted. The correct carrier of a ratification is the orchestrator's record, not the ratified attempt's own evidence directory. Same reason as T1-14 (binding.json is a frozen artifact under review_pending).
